docs.title: lowpass1
docs.text:
class lowpass1

A class of first-order lowpass filter that can smoothes the input signal.

This filter smoothes the input signal using filter coefficients and past output values to generate an output signal with high frequency components removed.

The smoothed output, filter coefficients, and past output are expressed by following formura.

\(y[t] = c_1 x[t] + c_2 x[t-1] + c_3 y[t-1]\).

  • \([t]\) : Time step
  • \(y[t]\) : Smoothed output that removed high frequency components.
  • \(x[t]\) : Input signal that includes high frequency components.
  • \(c_1\)~\(c_3\) : Coefficients of the filter.

docs.title: calc_filter_coefficients
docs.text:
std::vector<double> calc_filter_coefficients(const double cutoff_freq, const double sample_freq)

Calculates three coefficients of filter from cut-off frequency and * sampling frequency.

Parameter cutoff_freq cut-off frequency [Hz]. Parameter sample_freq samplilng frequency to observe data [Hz]. Return Three coefficients of filter. Values for c1 to c3 in the below equation. y[t] = c1 * x[t] + c2 * x[t-1] + c3 * y[t-1]

docs.title: continuous_frequency_represent
docs.text:
std::complex<double> continuous_frequency_represent(const double omega)

Returns the magnitude and phase at specified omega [rad/s] as the continuous system.

When w[rad/s] is specified, {real, imag} of G(jw) is returned with following equation. G(jw) = real + j * imag real = 1 / (1 + w^2 * T^2) imag = (-wT) / (1 + w^2 * T^2)

Parameter omega Angular velocity [rad/s] that you want to know the filter frequency response. Return frequency response with specified w. Returned value is represents with complex type.

docs.title: frequency_response
docs.text:
std::tuple<std::vector<double>, std::vector<double>, std::vector<double>> frequency_response(std::vector<double> omega)

calculates multiple frequency responsese of the filter.

Parameter omega This vector contains the frequencies for which you want to know the frequency response of the filter. Return Three vectors reresent magnitude, phase, and, anguler frequency respectively. Anguler frequencies are sorted in ascending order. The magnitude and phase contains the frequency response correspoing to omega. For example, the response at omega.at(2) is in magnitude.at(2) and phase.at(2).

docs.title: get_filter_params
docs.text:
std::tuple<std::vector<double>, std::vector<double>> get_filter_params()

Returns coefficients and parameters of the filter.

double cutoff_freq = 5;
double sample_freq = 100;

syscon::lowpass1 filter(cutoff_freq, sample_freq);
auto [coefficients, parameters] = filter.get_filter_params();

std::cout << "y[t] = coefficients.at(0) << "x[t] + " << coefficients.at(1) << "x[t-1] + " << coefficients.at(2) << "y[t-1]" << std::endl;
std::cout << "[sampling period] = " << parameters.at(0) << " [s]" << std::endl;
std::cout << "[time constant  ] = " << parameters.at(1) << " [s]" << std::endl;

----------------------
y[t] = 0.135755 x[t] + 0.135755 x[t-1] + 0.72849 y[t-1]
[sampling period   ] = 0.01s
[time constant     ] = 0.031831s
Return Returns coefficients and parameters of the low pass filter.

  • Coefficients of the filter (\(c_1\)~\(c_3\)) in \(y[t] = c_1 x[t] + c_2 x[t-1] + c_3 y[t-1]\).

  • Time parameters of the filter : Sampling period [s] and time constant [s].

docs.text:
lowpass1()

The constructor of a low pass filter of first-order system.

This constructor dose not take any arguments, so use lowpass1::set_filter_params() to pass the filter parameter before you use this filter.

lowpass1(const double cutoff_freq, const double sample_freq)

The constructor of a low pass filter of first-order system.

This constructor takes all the information needed to user the filter. Then, it calculates the filter coefficients internally.

double cut_off_frequency = 20; //20Hz
double sampling_frequency = 100; // 100Hz

syscon::lowpass1 filter(cut_off_frequency, sampling_frequency);
Parameter cutoff_freq The cut off frequency [Hz] Parameter sample_freq sampling frequency [Hz]

docs.title: step
docs.text:
double step(const double observed_x)

Returns a signal that high frequency components removed.

Parameter observed_x The new input for this filter. This value is observed by a sensor, etc., and includes high frequency components. 
syscon::lowpass1 filter(20, 100);
while(true)
{
sensor_signal = get_sensor_data();
signal = filter.step(sensor_signal);
}
Return A signal from witch frequency components more than the cutoff frequency is removed.
